newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Nokia rises in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Nokia rises in New York.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications company Nokia Group rose Monday to highlight trade in foreign shares and American Depositary Receipts ADRs.
Traders said European ADRs were helped by the stronger dollar, now close to a four-year high against the Japanese yen. The rising dollar is good news for European exporters.
"Everything is looking a bit upbeat. The dollar is the key that has made everything go better here," an ADR trader said.

ADRs in Nokia rose 1-3/8 to 59 after the company announced it had entered a joint venture with Oracle Corp to build a system allowing Internet access from any Nokia Global System for Mobile communication phone with messaging capability.
Goldman Sachs also raised its rating for Nokia to trading buy from market outperformer.
Shares in troubled Canadian gold mining company Bre-X fell 7/16 to 1-15/16 as Canadian traders said institutional investors were shedding the stock.
Trade was heavy and the company, hit by questions about an Indonesian deposit, was the most active among foreign issues.

Brazilian telephone holding company Telebras SA rose 2-1/2 to a record 118 after the government received bids for private cellular telephone concessions. The ADRs also have been boosted by recent rate increases.

The bidding "is helping the whole privatization process go forward," a traders said. "Telebras is big, it's big with the end of growth in the United States" markets as investors look to diversify their portfolios.
Other Latin American telecommunications ADRs also rose. Telefonos de Mexico was up 3/4 to 40-1/8, Telecom Argentina rose 5/8 to 45-1/2 and Telefonica de Argentina was up 1/4 to 29-7/8.
Advancers led decliners 262 to 160 amid 806 ADRs. The ADR index rose 0.37 percent and volume in late morning was 24 million shares.
